verdicts.title: Quantum State Designs from Minimally Random Quantum Circuits
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Random many-body states are both a useful tool to model certain physical systems and an important asset for quantum computation. Realising them, however, generally requires an exponential (in system size) amount of resources. Recent research has presented a way out by showing that one can generate random states, or more precisely a controlled approximation of them, by applying a quantum circuit built in terms of few-body unitary gates. verdicts.title: Quantum Qomrades: Catalysts in Resource Theories and Memories in Dynamic Programming
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Quantum information theory explores the limits of manipulating quantum states. While auxiliary systems often enhance information processing, a systematic explanation for their power has been lacking. This thesis addresses this gap by investigating the underlying sources of strength in using auxiliary systems. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses catalysts and auxiliary memory states achieving 'exponential reduction in circuit depth at the cost of increased width,' which concerns quantum algorithm design rather than any holographic entanglement rank bound on Boolean circuit depth. It shares the vocabulary of 'circuit depth' but does not address HER(C) = Θ(D).
